sentences.text: Shri Kuldeep Singh Rajpoot - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Amit Bhurrak - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State
 Order

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.195/2023 registered at Police Station Shivpur, District Narmadapuram, for the offences punishable under Sections 366,
376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4, 5, 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 26.11.2024.

2. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that though the applicant has been implicated in the alleged offence, but he has already entered into marriage with the prosecutrix and this fact can be ascertained from her statement recorded under Section 164 of the CrPC.
It is further submitted that at present the prosecutrix is residing in her in-laws house.

It is further submitted that under such circumstances, keeping the applicant behind the bars would not serve any fruitful purpose and as such, it is prayed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12621 2 MCRC-10748-2025 that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
3. On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer of bail and read over the case diary.

4. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of case Rupesh Jadam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34353492/
1 diary especially the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of the CrPC, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.

entities.text: Rupesh Jadam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case,
this application is allowed.

5. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.
6. On being released, the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
